extracted_content: BlindFed's empirical evaluation across CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and SVHN demonstrates that it achieves accuracy closely matching full fine-tuning and LoRA while strictly adhering to double-blind privacy constraints. In centralized settings, BlindFed reaches 94.28% accuracy on CIFAR-10 and 92.32% on SVHN, significantly outperforming linear probing (92.26% and 59.38% respectively). In federated scenarios with varying data heterogeneity (Dirichlet alpha = 100 to 0.01), BlindFed maintains robust performance, often outperforming LoRA in highly heterogeneous cases (alpha=0.01). The addition of Stochastic Block Sampling (SBS) for enhanced privacy has a negligible impact on accuracy, and in some instances, slightly improves generalization. Scalability results on CIFAR-10 show that BlindFed remains effective as the number of clients increases from 10 to 50, consistently outperforming linear probing. Efficiency metrics reveal that BlindFed operates with a latency only ~4% higher than linear probing while requiring significantly less GPU memory than full fine-tuning or LoRA.

key_figures.caption: Comparison of the efficiency of different adaptation methods in terms of the number of parameters, latency, and memory usage across three datasets: CIFAR-10/SVHN, CIFAR-100, and Fed-ISIC2019.
key_figures.relevance: Visualizes the trade-off between performance and efficiency, showing BlindFed's near-optimal latency and low memory footprint.

key_tables.caption: Comparison of accuracy achieved by our proposed method against baseline approaches on three datasets (CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and SVHN) in both centralized and federated learning scenarios.
key_tables.relevance: Provides the core accuracy results proving BlindFed is comparable to non-private baselines like LoRA and superior to linear probing.

key_tables.caption: Performance comparison of our method with baseline approaches on the Fed-ISIC2019 dataset with five clients (K = 5), using two auxiliary datasets: Fed-ISIC2019 (center=0) as an in-distribution (InD) dataset and Tiny-ImageNet as an out-of-distribution (OOD) dataset.
key_tables.relevance: Shows the framework's effectiveness on medical imaging tasks and its robustness to different auxiliary datasets used during distillation.

key_tables.caption: Scalability analysis of the proposed method to baseline approaches on the CIFAR-10 dataset, with varying number of clients K ∈ {10, 20, 50} under a Dirichlet concentration parameter of 1.0 for data partitioning.
key_tables.relevance: Demonstrates that BlindFed scales effectively to a larger number of clients without significant performance degradation.
